subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Action-Packed Verb Adventure
hook: Discover verbs — the words that show action and movement!

slides.title: Arun and Maya's Action-Packed Verb Adventure
What is a Verb?
slides.storyContext: Arun jumps and says 'Jump! That's a verb — an action word!' Maya runs and shouts 'Run!'

points.label: Verb
points.text: A word that shows action or what someone does

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs are action words that show doing!

slides.title: Understanding Action Verbs

points.label: Action verbs
points.text: Show what a person or thing DOES

points.label: Examples
points.text: jump, run, walk, skip, dance, throw, catch, swim, fly

slides.inSimpleWords: Action verbs show movement and doing!

slides.title: Run, Jump, Eat, Sleep
slides.storyContext: Maya makes a list: 'I run, I jump, I eat, I sleep — all verbs that show what I do!'

points.label: Action verbs
points.text: run, jump, eat, sleep, play, walk, dance, sing

slides.inSimpleWords: Run, jump, eat are all action verbs!

slides.title: Action Verbs in Daily Life
slides.storyContext: Arun shows verbs he does every day!

example.problem: Name 5 things you do every day.
example.solution: I wake up, I eat breakfast, I walk to school, I play, I sleep. (wake, eat, walk, play, sleep are all verbs)

slides.inSimpleWords: Every day is full of action verbs!

slides.title: Write, Read, Draw, Think
slides.storyContext: Arun does homework: 'I write answers, I read questions, I draw pictures, I think carefully!'

points.label: Action verbs
points.text: write, read, draw, think, learn, understand, remember

slides.inSimpleWords: Write, read, draw, think show different actions!

slides.title: Mental Action Verbs

points.label: Mental verbs
points.text: Show thinking and learning, not just physical movement

points.label: Examples
points.text: think, know, believe, remember, forget, understand, learn, plan

slides.inSimpleWords: Some verbs show what our brain does!

slides.title: Can, Help, Give, Take
slides.storyContext: Maya helps Arun: 'I can lift this! I help my friend! I give him a pencil. He takes it!'

points.label: More verbs
points.text: can, help, give, take, make, build, break, fix

slides.inSimpleWords: Help, give, take show actions between people!

slides.title: Verbs in School and Home
slides.storyContext: Maya shows verbs used in school and at home!

example.problem: Write 3 verbs from school and 3 from home.
example.solution: School: write, read, listen. Home: cook, clean, play. (all are verbs)

slides.inSimpleWords: We use different verbs in different places!

slides.title: Find the Hidden Verbs
slides.storyContext: Maya makes sentences and Arun finds the verbs!

points.text: The cat sleeps. / She drinks milk. / They run fast.

slides.inSimpleWords: Can you spot which word is the verb?

slides.title: Being Verbs: Is, Are, Am, Was, Were
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'I am happy. She is smart. They are friends. I was sleepy. We were tired!'

points.label: Being verbs
points.text: is, are, am, was, were (show state of being, not action)

points.label: What they do
points.text: Show who or what something IS, not what it DOES

slides.inSimpleWords: Being verbs show who or what something is!

image.alt: Being Verbs: Is, Are, Am, Was, Were — Verbs

slides.title: Different Forms of Being

points.label: am
points.text: I am (singular, for 'I')

points.label: is
points.text: He/She/It is (singular)

points.label: are
points.text: You/We/They are (plural)

slides.inSimpleWords: Being verbs change with who is doing it!

slides.title: Verbs in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write sentences using different verbs!

example.problem: Complete these: The cat ___. The boy ___. She ___ milk.
example.solution: The cat sleeps. The boy plays. She drinks milk. (sleeps, plays, drinks are verbs)

slides.inSimpleWords: Every sentence needs a verb to show action!

slides.title: Being Verbs in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Maya writes sentences with being verbs!

example.problem: Fill in: ___ am happy. ___ is tall. ___ are friends.
example.solution: I am happy. He is tall. We are friends. (am, is, are show what they ARE)

slides.inSimpleWords: Being verbs tell us how people are!

slides.title: Action or Being Verb?
slides.storyContext: Arun asks: Is this an action or being verb?

points.text: jump, is, run, are, eat, am, dance, was

slides.inSimpleWords: Can you sort action and being verbs?

slides.title: Verbs Can Change
slides.storyContext: Maya shows: 'I play today. I played yesterday. I will play tomorrow. The verb changes with time!'

points.label: Verb tenses
points.text: play (now), played (past), will play (future)

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs change when we talk about different times!

slides.title: Present, Past, and Future Verbs

points.label: Present
points.text: play, eat, run (happening NOW)

points.label: Past
points.text: played, ate, ran (already happened)

points.label: Future
points.text: will play, will eat, will run (will happen)

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs show when things happen!

slides.title: One Verb, Three Times
slides.storyContext: Maya shows how one verb changes!

example.problem: Write 'run' in past, present, and future.
example.solution: I ran yesterday. I run today. I will run tomorrow. (past, present, future)

slides.inSimpleWords: One verb can show three different times!

slides.title: Change the Verb Tense
slides.storyContext: Arun challenges you to change verbs!

points.text: I play. (Change to past) → I played. / She runs. (Change to future) → She will run.

slides.inSimpleWords: Can you change verbs to past and future?

slides.title: Verb Power: Making Sentences Complete

points.label: Rule
points.text: Every sentence MUST have a verb

points.label: Why
points.text: Without a verb, we don't know what is happening!

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs are the most important words!

slides.title: Verbs Come After Nouns

points.label: Pattern
points.text: Noun + Verb (The dog + runs)

points.label: Examples
points.text: The cat sleeps. The boy plays. She sings.

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs tell what the noun does!

slides.title: Verbs in Our Lives
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya show verbs they use every day: wake, eat, go, learn, play, sleep!

points.label: Daily verbs
points.text: wake, eat, go, learn, play, sleep, drink, sit, stand, walk

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs are everywhere in our lives!

slides.title: My Day in Verbs
slides.storyContext: Arun describes his whole day using verbs!

example.problem: Write about your day using action verbs.
example.solution: I wake up, I eat breakfast, I go to school, I learn, I play, I come home, I do homework, I sleep.

slides.inSimpleWords: Every part of your day has a verb!

slides.title: Verbs Show Movement and State

points.label: Movement verbs
points.text: run, jump, walk, swim, fly (show action)

points.label: State verbs
points.text: is, am, are (show being or condition)

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs can show doing or being!

slides.title: Verbs Show Action
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya make a poster of all their favorite action verbs!

points.label: Action verbs
points.text: run, jump, eat, write, read, play, dance, sing

points.label: Being verbs
points.text: is, are, am, was, were

points.label: Verb tenses
points.text: present, past, future (changes with time)

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs are the most important words in sentences!

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Describing Word Adventure
hook: Learn adjectives — words that describe how things look, feel, and are!

slides.title: Arun and Maya's Describing Word Adventure
What is an Adjective?
slides.storyContext: Arun holds a big red apple. 'Big and red — these words describe the apple!' says Maya.

points.label: Adjective
points.text: A word that describes a noun (how it looks, feels, or is)

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives are describing words for nouns!

slides.title: Adjectives Answer Questions

points.label: Adjectives answer
points.text: WHAT KIND? HOW MANY? WHAT COLOR? HOW DOES IT FEEL?

points.label: Adjectives modify
points.text: Nouns — they describe people, places, and things

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives tell us more about nouns!

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Size
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'This is a big house. This is a small house. Big and small describe size!'

points.label: Size adjectives
points.text: big, small, large, tiny, huge, long, short, wide, narrow

slides.inSimpleWords: Big, small, tiny describe how big something is!

slides.title: Using Size Adjectives
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya describe different things!

example.problem: Describe: a book, a dog, a pencil using size adjectives.
example.solution: a small book, a big dog, a long pencil. (small, big, long are adjectives)

slides.inSimpleWords: Size adjectives tell how big or small!

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Color
slides.storyContext: Maya paints: 'A red heart, a blue sky, a yellow sun, a green tree!'

points.label: Color adjectives
points.text: red, blue, yellow, green, orange, purple, pink, black, white

slides.inSimpleWords: Red, blue, green describe the color of things!

slides.title: Color Words Are Adjectives

points.label: Color adjectives
points.text: Describe what color a noun is

points.label: Order matters
points.text: big red apple (size + color + noun)

slides.inSimpleWords: Colors describe things we see!

slides.title: Pick the Color Adjective
slides.storyContext: Maya asks: Which word describes the color?

points.text: pink flower, blue sky, green grass, orange carrot

slides.inSimpleWords: Can you spot the color words?

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Feelings
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'I feel happy. The movie is funny. The noise is loud and scary!'

points.label: Feeling adjectives
points.text: happy, sad, funny, scary, brave, shy, angry, friendly

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives can describe feelings too!

slides.title: Feeling Adjectives in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya describe how people feel!

example.problem: Describe your friend using a feeling adjective.
example.solution: My friend is kind. My friend is funny. (kind, funny describe how they are)

slides.inSimpleWords: Feeling words describe people!

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Texture and Taste
slides.storyContext: Maya touches a smooth silk cloth and a rough rope. Arun tastes sweet candy and sour lemon!

points.label: Texture/taste
points.text: soft, hard, smooth, rough, wet, dry, sweet, sour, spicy, delicious

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives describe how things feel and taste!

image.alt: Adjectives Describe Texture and Taste — Adjectives

slides.title: Touch and Taste Adjectives
slides.storyContext: Maya touches things and tastes things!

points.text: soft pillow, rough rope, sweet candy, salty chip

slides.inSimpleWords: Can you describe how things feel?

slides.title: Using Adjectives in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write sentences with lots of describing words!

example.problem: Write: 'I have a dog.' Add adjectives to make it more interesting.
example.solution: I have a big, brown, friendly dog. (big, brown, friendly are adjectives)

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives make sentences more interesting!

slides.title: Make Sentences More Interesting
slides.storyContext: Maya wants you to add adjectives!

points.text: The house is big. The apple is red and sweet. The dog is small.

slides.inSimpleWords: Add describing words to make it better!

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Numbers and More
slides.storyContext: Maya says: 'I have one apple, three books, many toys, few pencils, first place, last runner!'

points.label: More adjectives
points.text: one, two, many, few, first, last, new, old, good, bad, beautiful, ugly

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives describe numbers and qualities too!

image.alt: Adjectives Describe Numbers and More — Adjectives

slides.title: Quality and Number Adjectives

points.label: Number adjectives
points.text: one, two, many, few, first, last (tell HOW MANY)

points.label: Quality adjectives
points.text: good, bad, beautiful, ugly, new, old (tell WHAT KIND)

slides.inSimpleWords: Numbers and qualities are adjectives!

slides.title: Number and Quality Adjectives
slides.storyContext: Arun shows both types!

example.problem: Write sentences with number and quality adjectives.
example.solution: I have three good friends. There are many beautiful flowers. (three, many = number; good, beautiful = quality)

slides.inSimpleWords: Both types make sentences better!

slides.title: Where Adjectives Go in Sentences

points.label: Before noun
points.text: big apple, blue sky, happy child (adjective comes BEFORE noun)

points.label: After 'is'
points.text: The apple is big. The sky is blue. (adjective comes AFTER being verbs)

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives can come before or after verbs!

slides.title: Opposite Adjectives
slides.storyContext: Maya shows pairs of opposite adjectives: big-small, happy-sad, hot-cold, clean-dirty!

points.label: Opposite pairs
points.text: big-small, happy-sad, hot-cold, clean-dirty, fast-slow, young-old

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives can have opposites!

slides.title: Using Opposite Adjectives
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya use opposites in sentences!

example.problem: Write an opposite for each adjective: The house is big. The box is heavy.
example.solution: The house is small. The box is light. (big-small, heavy-light are opposites)

slides.inSimpleWords: Opposites help us describe better!

slides.title: Adjectives Make Writing Better

points.label: Without adjectives
points.text: I have a dog.

points.label: With adjectives
points.text: I have a big, brown, friendly dog that is very playful!

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives make stories more colorful!

slides.title: Adjectives Describe Everything
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write a colorful story full of describing words!

points.label: Size and shape
points.text: big, small, long, short, round, square

points.label: Color
points.text: red, blue, green, yellow, orange, purple

points.label: Feelings and qualities
points.text: happy, sad, beautiful, ugly, good, bad, brave, shy

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives make describing easier and fun!

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Time Travel Tenses
hook: Journey through past, present, and future with verbs that change with time!

slides.title: Arun and Maya's Time Travel Tenses
What is Tense?
slides.storyContext: Arun explains: 'Tense shows WHEN an action happens — now, yesterday, or tomorrow!'

points.label: Tense
points.text: The time when an action happens (past, present, or future)

slides.inSimpleWords: Tense tells us WHEN something happens!

slides.title: Three Times for Verbs

points.label: Past
points.text: Something that already happened (yesterday, last week, last year)

points.label: Present
points.text: Something happening RIGHT NOW (today, this moment)

points.label: Future
points.text: Something that will happen (tomorrow, next week, later)

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs show three different times!

slides.title: Present Tense: Right Now
slides.storyContext: Maya says: 'I play now. I eat now. I read now. This is PRESENT TENSE!'

points.label: Present tense
points.text: Action happening RIGHT NOW: play, eat, read, run, jump, sing

slides.inSimpleWords: Present tense = action happening RIGHT NOW!

image.alt: Present Tense: Right Now — Tenses Basic

slides.title: Present Tense Examples
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya show present tense verbs!

example.problem: What are you doing RIGHT NOW? Use present tense.
example.solution: I sit in class. I listen to the teacher. I write in my notebook. (sit, listen, write are present tense)

slides.inSimpleWords: Present tense tells what's happening now!

slides.title: Time Words for Present

points.label: Now
points.text: right now, today, at this moment

points.label: Today words
points.text: every day, always, usually, often

slides.inSimpleWords: These time words go with present tense!

slides.title: Past Tense: Yesterday
slides.storyContext: Arun remembers: 'I played yesterday. I ate yesterday. I read yesterday. This is PAST TENSE!'

points.label: Past tense
points.text: Action that already happened: played, ate, read, ran, jumped, sang

slides.inSimpleWords: Past tense = action that already happened!

slides.title: Forming Past Tense

points.label: Regular verbs
points.text: Add 'ed' at the end: play → played, walk → walked, jump → jumped

points.label: Irregular verbs
points.text: Change completely: eat → ate, go → went, run → ran

slides.inSimpleWords: Past tense verbs often end with 'ed'!

slides.title: Past Tense Examples
slides.storyContext: Maya tells about yesterday!

example.problem: What did you do yesterday? Use past tense.
example.solution: I played with my friend. I ate lunch. I did homework. (played, ate, did are past tense)

slides.inSimpleWords: Past tense talks about what already happened!

slides.title: Time Words for Past

points.label: Yesterday
points.text: yesterday, last week, last year, before

points.label: Before words
points.text: ago, in the past, long ago

slides.inSimpleWords: These time words go with past tense!

slides.title: Future Tense: Tomorrow
slides.storyContext: Maya dreams: 'I will play tomorrow. I will eat tomorrow. I will read tomorrow. FUTURE TENSE!'

points.label: Future tense
points.text: Action that will happen: will play, will eat, will read, will run

slides.inSimpleWords: Future tense = action that will happen!

slides.title: Forming Future Tense

points.label: Future tense
points.text: Start with 'will' + the base form of the verb

points.label: Formula
points.text: will + play, will + eat, will + run, will + read

slides.inSimpleWords: Future uses 'will' + the verb!

slides.title: Guess the Future Plan
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya tell their plans!

points.text: I will visit my grandma. / She will play basketball. / They will study for the test.

slides.inSimpleWords: Can you spot the future tense verbs?

slides.title: Time Words for Future

points.label: Tomorrow
points.text: tomorrow, next week, next year, later

points.label: Future words
points.text: soon, in the future, will, going to

slides.inSimpleWords: These time words go with future tense!

slides.title: How Verbs Change with Tense
slides.storyContext: Arun shows how the same action verb changes: play (now), played (before), will play (later)!

points.label: Present
points.text: play, eat, run, read

points.label: Past
points.text: played, ate, ran, read

points.label: Future
points.text: will play, will eat, will run, will read

slides.inSimpleWords: The same verb changes form for each time!

image.alt: How Verbs Change with Tense — Tenses Basic

slides.title: Using All Three Tenses
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write about the same action in past, present, and future!

example.problem: Write sentences with 'eat': past, now, and future.
example.solution: I ate rice yesterday. I eat rice today. I will eat rice tomorrow. (ate, eat, will eat)

slides.inSimpleWords: Same verb, different tense = different time!

image.alt: Using All Three Tenses — Tenses Basic

slides.title: Change the Tense
slides.storyContext: Maya challenges you to write all three tenses!

points.text: I walk to school. (Write in past and future) → I walked to school. / I will walk to school.

slides.inSimpleWords: Can you write past, present, and future?

slides.title: Irregular Verbs: Special Ones
slides.storyContext: Maya shows verbs that don't follow the normal rules: go/went/will go, eat/ate/will eat, run/ran/will run!

points.label: Irregular verbs
points.text: go→went, eat→ate, run→ran, is→was, have→had (don't add 'ed')

slides.inSimpleWords: Some verbs change in special ways in past!

image.alt: Irregular Verbs: Special Ones — Tenses Basic

slides.title: Common Irregular Verbs

points.label: go
points.text: go (now) → went (past) → will go (future)

points.label: eat
points.text: eat (now) → ate (past) → will eat (future)

points.label: run
points.text: run (now) → ran (past) → will run (future)

points.label: see
points.text: see (now) → saw (past) → will see (future)

slides.inSimpleWords: Irregular verbs are unique!

slides.title: Using Irregular Verbs
slides.storyContext: Arun uses irregular verbs in sentences!

example.problem: Write 'go' in past, present, and future.
example.solution: I go to school today. I went to school yesterday. I will go to school tomorrow.

slides.inSimpleWords: Irregular verbs are important to learn!

slides.title: Same Story, Three Times

points.label: Past: I went.
points.text: Something already happened

points.label: Present: I go.
points.text: Something happening now

points.label: Future: I will go.
points.text: Something will happen

slides.inSimpleWords: One sentence, three tenses!

slides.title: Tense Markers in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Maya points to words that show time: yesterday, today, tomorrow, long ago, soon!

points.label: Time clues
points.text: yesterday (past), today (present), tomorrow (future), last week, next week, soon, long ago

slides.inSimpleWords: Time words tell us the tense!

slides.title: My Tense Timeline
slides.storyContext: Arun makes a timeline of his actions!

example.problem: Write about what you did, do, and will do.
example.solution: I played yesterday. I play today. I will play tomorrow. (All show the same action in three times)

slides.inSimpleWords: Your life has past, present, and future!

slides.title: Three Tenses, Three Times
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya create a timeline showing past, present, and future actions!

points.label: Past tense
points.text: Yesterday: I played, I ate, I ran, I read

points.label: Present tense
points.text: Now: I play, I eat, I run, I read

points.label: Future tense
points.text: Tomorrow: I will play, I will eat, I will run

slides.inSimpleWords: Past = done. Present = now. Future = coming soon!

image.alt: Three Tenses, Three Times — Tenses Basic
